findings.who: A filer who sold all their stock in December 2024 after the ex-dividend date, so the dividend was paid in January 2025. Their 2025 Form 1099-DIV arrived in February 2026.
findings.why_no: "In 2025" governs both clauses. The filer owned no shares in 2025 and got the Form 1099-DIV in 2026, not in 2025. Every Form 1099-DIV for 2025 arrives in 2026, so the "get a Form 1099-DIV" clause, read literally, never yields a yes.
findings.line: sb.ordinary_dividends_if_dividends (also div.box12_if_dividends and sd.distributions_if_dividends for fund shares sold before 2025 with a January 2025 payout)
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends. This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements."
findings.fix: Ask: "At any time in 2024 or 2025, did you (or your spouse) own shares outside a retirement account, or did you receive any dividend or distribution in 2025, or get a Form 1099-DIV for 2025 (it arrives in early 2026)?"

findings.who: A shareholder whose company dissolved and cancelled its shares in 2024, and who received the final cash or property liquidation distribution, or a return of capital, in 2025.
findings.why_no: The shares no longer existed in 2025, so the filer did not "own shares" then. The form, if any, came in 2026.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: "Boxes 9 and 10. Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions." "Box 3. Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain."
findings.fix: Add "or receive any payment from a company or fund, including a payout when it closed or a return of capital" to the gate.

findings.who: A filer who is the actual owner of shares held in a parent's or sibling's name, or who owns part of an account whose Form 1099-DIV is issued to another person's SSN.
findings.why_no: The account and the form are in someone else's name, so the filer reads "own shares" and "get a Form 1099-DIV" as no. Only the gated questions' help mentions amounts paid in someone else's name; the gate's help does not.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Nominees: "If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient."; i1040sb p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends."
findings.fix: Add to the gate: "Include shares or accounts held in someone else's name that are partly or wholly yours."

findings.who: A filer whose only investment is 'cash' at a brokerage or robo-advisor that is swept into a money market fund, and whose statement calls the payouts 'interest'. The fund may be a tax-exempt one paying box 12 amounts.
findings.why_no: The filer believes they hold cash, not 'shares of a fund'. The statement is titled 'Consolidated 1099' or says 'interest', not Form 1099-DIV. The gate's help names money market funds, but the filer does not know they hold one.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: "Box 12. Shows exempt-interest dividends from a mutual fund or other RIC paid to you"; i1040sb p. 2: "This amount should be shown in box 1a of your Forms 1099-DIV or substitute statements."
findings.fix: Add to the gate: "or have a brokerage, robo-advisor or investment app account (even one holding only cash), or get any statement from such an account".

findings.who: A filer holding units of a unit investment trust (for example a municipal bond UIT), or interests in a non-traded REIT bought through an app. Some such REITs retain gains and send Form 2439.
findings.why_no: They hold 'units' or 'interests', not 'shares of a company or a fund'. The gate's help lists only stocks, mutual funds, ETFs and money market funds.
findings.irs_text: i1040sd p. 6: "Include on Schedule D, line 11, the amount from box 1a of Form 2439... the regulated investment company (including a mutual fund) or real estate investment trust."
findings.fix: Add to the gate's help: "Units of a unit investment trust and shares or interests in a REIT (traded or not) also count."

findings.who: A filer saving for retirement in an ordinary taxable brokerage account they call their 'retirement account'.
findings.why_no: "Outside a retirement account": the filer thinks their only shares are inside one.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Line 5: "Report on line 5 all of your ordinary dividends."
findings.fix: Say "outside an IRA, 401(k), 403(b) or other tax-deferred plan; a regular brokerage account counts even if you are saving it for retirement".

findings.who: An ESOP participant, or the beneficiary of one, to whom the employer paid dividends on plan shares directly in cash, where the 1099-DIV is misplaced or not yet in hand.
findings.why_no: The shares are in a retirement plan (the ESOP), so "outside a retirement account" is a truthful no. The form clause then depends on the filer having the form.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 1b: "The amount shown may be dividends a corporation paid directly to you as a participant (or beneficiary of a participant) in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). Report it as a dividend on your Form 1040"
findings.fix: Add: "or receive cash dividends paid directly to you on shares in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP)".

findings.who: A filer whose mutual fund or REIT shares are held through a nominee, such as a relative, an informal partnership or an investment club. The nominee did not furnish the filer a Form 1099-DIV, so the filer has a capital gain distribution, entered in box 2a under the 'amounts received without a form' help, part of which is unrecaptured section 1250, section 1202 or collectibles gain.
findings.why_no: The gate asks about 'an amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of any Form 1099-DIV'. The filer received no Form 1099-DIV, so the truthful answer is no. Yet the box 2a question invited them to enter amounts received without a form, so box 2a is above zero.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2b. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain…'; 'Nominees. If this form includes amounts belonging to another person … you must furnish a Form 1099-DIV to each.'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact, not the form: 'Was any part of your or your spouse's capital gain distributions (from a form, a nominee's statement, or with no form at all) reported or identified as unrecaptured section 1250 gain, section 1202 gain, or collectibles (28%) gain, or did you have a nondividend (return of capital) distribution, a liquidation distribution, or AMT exempt-interest dividends?'

findings.who: A filer who owns a share of a fund held in someone else's name, such as a parent's or co-owner's account under that person's TIN. The Form 1099-DIV for the account, issued to the other person, shows amounts in boxes 2a and 2b.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'of any Form 1099-DIV' together with the gate's 'you or your spouse … received a Form 1099-DIV' as limited to forms issued to them. They check only their own forms, which have nothing in the less common boxes. Their own forms may show box 2a but nothing else.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2b. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is unrecaptured section 1250 gain…'; 'Box 2c. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is section 1202 gain…'; 'Box 2d. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is 28% rate gain…'
findings.fix: Add the gated questions' help to the gate: 'Include forms issued in someone else's name for amounts that are partly yours, and any amounts received without a form.'

findings.who: A filer whose dividends come on a broker's composite statement, a substitute form that labels lines by description ('Unrecap. Sec. 1250 gain', 'Collectibles (28%) gain', 'Nondividend distributions') rather than by box number. Or a filer with a corrected Form 1099-DIV that adds a box 2b amount the original form left blank.
findings.why_no: The filer looks for numbered boxes 2b, 2c, 2d, 3, 9, 10 or 13 on 'a Form 1099-DIV'. They do not treat the composite statement as that form, or they consult only the original form they received first.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 2d. Shows the portion of the amount in box 2a that is 28% rate gain from sales or exchanges of collectibles. If required, use this amount when completing the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet…'
findings.fix: Name the boxes by their captions along with their numbers. Add: 'including a broker's combined (composite) statement and any corrected form; use the latest corrected amounts.'

findings.who: A filer or spouse who received qualified dividends that no Form 1099-DIV reports. Examples: dividends from a foreign corporation held directly with no U.S. payer, dividends under the payer's reporting threshold, or qualified dividends passed through on a Schedule K-1 from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust.
findings.why_no: The gate totals 'Form 1099-DIV box 1a'. With no Form 1099-DIV, that total is truthfully zero, so the tool computes the condition as false and never asks for qualified dividends.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 26, Line 3a: "See Pub. 550 for the definition of qualified dividends if you received dividends not reported on Form 1099-DIV." Also p. 25: "Generally, these dividends are shown in box 1b of Form(s) 1099-DIV."
findings.fix: Base the gate on the fact, not the form: 'Did you or your spouse receive any dividends in 2025, from any source (Form 1099-DIV, Schedule K-1, a foreign company, or with no form at all)?' Then ask for qualified dividends from each source, not only box 1b.

findings.who: A parent who elects Form 8814 to report a child's dividends on the parent's return, while neither spouse has dividends of their own.
findings.why_no: The question is whether 'you or your spouse received dividends'. The child received them, so the truthful answer is no, and the parent's box 1a total is zero. Line 3a never picks up the child's qualified dividends.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 25, Line 3a: "If you are including your child's qualified dividends in the total on line 3a, check box 1 on line 3c. For more information, see the Instructions for Form 8814."
findings.fix: Also open the gate when the filer elects Form 8814 and the child had qualified dividends. Carry the child's qualified dividends into line 3a whether or not the parents had dividends of their own.

findings.who: An investor whose mutual fund, ETF or REIT dividends were reinvested automatically, so no cash was paid out to them.
findings.why_no: The words 'received dividends or other distributions' suggest money arriving. A filer who saw only extra shares may answer no, even though box 1a reports the reinvested amount.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: "Box 1a. Shows total ordinary dividends that are taxable. Include this amount on the 'Ordinary dividends' line of Form 1040"; "Box 5. Shows the portion of the amount in box 1a that may be eligible for the 20% qualified business income deduction under section 199A."
findings.fix: Add help text: 'Count dividends even if they were reinvested in more shares or kept in your brokerage account. If you got a Form 1099-DIV, or a consolidated 1099 with a dividends section, answer yes.'

findings.who: An employee who received dividends that a corporation paid directly on stock held in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP).
findings.why_no: The filer sees this money as a retirement-plan distribution rather than a dividend from an investment, so they answer no to 'dividends or other distributions'.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 1b: "The amount shown may be dividends a corporation paid directly to you as a participant (or beneficiary of a participant) in an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP). Report it as a dividend on your Form 1040 or 1040-SR"
findings.fix: Add to the gate help: 'Include dividends paid to you on employer stock in an ESOP, and any amount on a Form 1099-DIV, even if you think of it as a plan payment.'

findings.who: A filer whose broker issues one consolidated tax statement, with sections for 1099-B, 1099-INT and 1099-DIV, rather than a separate document titled Form 1099-DIV.
findings.why_no: The filer asks whether they got a 'Form 1099-DIV' and, finding no stand-alone form, answers no or enters zero for box 1a.
findings.irs_text: i1040gi p. 26, Line 3b: "Each payer should send you a Form 1099-DIV ... This amount should be shown in box 1a of Form(s) 1099-DIV."
findings.fix: Say that a 1099-DIV section inside a consolidated brokerage statement counts as a Form 1099-DIV.

used.how: pages named by another document's citation

findings.who: A filer whose Form 1099-DIV (or a spouse's, on a joint return) shows an amount in box 3. The filer, or both spouses, do not treat box 3 as one of the 'less common boxes'.
findings.why_no: The box 3 amount reaches the gate only through the parent helper, 'when a Form 1099-DIV shows an amount in one of the less common boxes.' A filer who sees boxes 1a, 1b, 2a and 3 on most fund statements, or who reads a list of 'less common' boxes as complete, answers no to the parent. Box 3 then stays zero and the gate is false.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain.'
findings.fix: Ask about box 3 directly for every Form 1099-DIV entered, and do not route it through a 'less common boxes' parent. Ask: 'Does box 3 (Nondividend distributions) on any Form 1099-DIV for you or your spouse show an amount above zero?'

findings.who: A filer holding a closed-end fund, REIT or other stock that paid a return of capital in 2025. Earlier returns of capital have already reduced the basis to zero.
findings.why_no: Box 3 is described as 'not taxable', so the filer sees no reason to report a nontaxable amount and leaves it out or answers no to the less-common-boxes parent. The help text does not say that box 3 can be taxable when it exceeds the remaining basis.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'To the extent of your cost (or other basis) in the stock, the distribution reduces your basis and is not taxable. Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain.'
findings.fix: In the help for the box 3 entry or the parent question, say: 'Enter box 3 even though it is often not taxable. It becomes taxable once it exceeds your remaining basis in the shares.'

findings.who: A filer or spouse who received a nondividend distribution (a return of capital in excess of the corporation's earnings) without a Form 1099-DIV. Examples are a payer that did not issue the form, a foreign corporation, or a closely held C corporation. Earlier distributions had already reduced the basis to zero.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed only from box 3 of a Form 1099-DIV. With no form there is truthfully no box 3 amount, so the gate is false and the basis question is never asked. The part above basis is a capital gain whether or not a form was issued, and the tool should refuse to complete the return.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5, Box 3: 'Shows a return of capital... Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain. See Pub. 550.'
findings.fix: Add a broad gate question: 'Did you or your spouse receive in 2025 any distribution that the payer described as a return of capital or nondividend distribution, whether or not it was reported in box 3 of a Form 1099-DIV?' Ask the basis question on a yes, or refuse when no amount is supplied.

findings.who: A shareholder of a small closely held C corporation, or of a foreign corporation, that paid a distribution exceeding its earnings and profits or a liquidating distribution in 2025, but issued no Form 1099-DIV.
findings.why_no: The filer answers yes to owning shares. The next question, 'An amount in box 2b, 2c, 2d, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of any Form 1099-DIV', is then truthfully no, because no form exists. The gated help would have told them to include 'any amount received without a form', but they never see it.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 3. Shows a return of capital. To the extent of your cost (or other basis) in the stock, the distribution reduces your basis and is not taxable. Any amount received in excess of your basis is taxable to you as capital gain.' 'Boxes 9 and 10. Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions.'
findings.fix: Ask about the fact, not the form: 'Did you or your spouse receive any distribution from a company or fund that was a return of capital (nondividend distribution), a liquidation distribution, or a private activity bond exempt-interest dividend, whether or not it was reported on a Form 1099-DIV, in boxes 2b, 2c, 2d, 3, 9, 10 or 13 of a Form 1099-DIV, or on a broker's or nominee's statement?'

findings.who: A former shareholder whose corporation adopted a plan of liquidation and cancelled the shares in 2024, and who received a further cash or property liquidation payment in 2025, with no 1099-DIV received or the form still pending.
findings.why_no: 'In 2025, did you ... own shares of a company or a fund' is truthfully no because the shares were gone before 2025. With no form in hand, 'or get a Form 1099-DIV' is also no.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Boxes 9 and 10. Show cash and noncash liquidation distributions.' The input help reads: 'Include ... any amount received without a form.'
findings.fix: Broaden the first gate: 'In 2025, did you (or your spouse) own shares of a company or fund outside a retirement account, receive any payment because of shares you own or once owned (including a liquidation payment), or get a Form 1099-DIV?'

findings.who: A filer whose shares are held in their revocable living trust, held by a nominee or relative in that person's name, or held in a custodial account, where the Form 1099-DIV is issued in the trust's or the other person's name.
findings.why_no: They read 'did you ... own shares' as no because the trust or the other person holds title, and 'get a Form 1099-DIV' as no because the form is in another name. The help text, 'Include your share of amounts paid in someone else's name', appears only after the gate.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Nominees. If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient ... to show their share of the income.' The input help reads: 'Include your share of amounts paid in someone else's name.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: '... including shares held for you in a trust you control, a custodial account, or another person's name, or a share of a Form 1099-DIV issued to someone else.'

findings.who: A filer with a tax-exempt municipal money market fund or a unit investment trust holding municipal bonds, who receives exempt-interest dividends that include private activity bond interest.
findings.why_no: They do not think of fund 'units' or a money market balance as 'shares of a company or a fund', and they treat tax-exempt income as nothing to report. If their statement is a combined broker statement, they may not recognize it as a Form 1099-DIV.
findings.irs_text: f1099div p. 5: 'Box 13. Shows exempt-interest dividends subject to the alternative minimum tax. This amount is included in box 12. See the Instructions for Form 6251.'
findings.fix: Name the cases in the gate: '... shares or units of a company, mutual fund, ETF, money market fund (including tax-exempt funds), REIT or unit investment trust ...'.
